# Zino3D

**Zino3D** is an offline-first, cross-platform 3D model editor. Import models generated by AI tools (Tripo AI
and others) or any GLB / glTF / OBJ / STL / FBX file, inspect and reorganise them, edit real mesh geometry —
for example split a car's wheels from its body — edit materials, and export clean GLB files.

- One React + TypeScript + Three.js codebase for browsers (desktop, tablet, phone), installable as a PWA,
  and packaged for iOS/iPadOS and Android with Capacitor.
- No account, no subscription, no cloud backend, no AI API, no analytics. Models are parsed on the device and
  never uploaded.

## Status

This is the first working release (v0.1). See [docs/LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md) for what is not done
yet, and the feature table below for what was implemented and how it is tested.

| Picking and multi-selection, transform gizmo (single & multi-object), snapping, world/local, 3D cursor                                                                                                 | ✅          | unit (commands), UI (selection)            |
| Hierarchy: select, multi/range select, rename, search, hide/show, lock, collections, group/ungroup, drag-to-reparent, context menu                                                                     | ✅          | unit + UI                                  |
| Numeric transforms, reset, apply (bake) transform, set origin (geometry center / bottom / cursor / world)                                                                                              | ✅          | unit + UI                                  |
| Undo/redo for every editing operation, bounded history (count + memory), GPU-resource cleanup                                                                                                          | ✅          | unit                                       |
| Edit Mode: vertex / edge / face selection, select all / none / invert / linked / by material, move vertices                                                                                            | ✅          | unit + UI                                  |

## Quick start

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev          # http://localhost:5173
npm test             # unit + integration tests (Vitest)
npm run build        # production build in dist/
npm run test:e2e     # UI tests (Playwright; builds must exist: run npm run build first)
```

Requires Node.js 20.19+ (CI uses Node 22).

## Using Zino3D (short version)

1. **Import** a model (button or drag & drop). For a `.gltf` that references `.bin`/texture files, select all of
   them together.
2. Pick objects in the viewport or the scene list. Move/rotate/scale with the gizmo or type exact values.
3. **Separate parts**: select a mesh → _Separate parts_ (every disconnected piece becomes an object) or the
   **Wheel & parts assistant** (ranks wheel-like pieces, previews them, lets you correct the choice).
   If wheels are fused into the body, use **Edit Mode → Face**, select the faces, and press **Separate (P)**.
4. Edit materials in the Properties panel. Shared materials are flagged; use _Make unique_ to edit one object only.
5. **Export** GLB. Separate objects stay separate nodes with their own transforms.

Everything is undoable (Ctrl/Cmd+Z). Projects autosave locally; use _Download project file_ for a portable backup.
